pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the seeded items are all 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
test/done.test.js 'AC-2' checks / and /?view=open list only the open items in id order.
test/done.test.js 'AC-3' marks ids 3 and 1 done and checks the order and the ✓ prefix.
test/done.test.js 'AC-4' checks all items, in id order, with ✓ only on done ones.
test/done.test.js 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and for /; the current view is a <strong>, not a link.
test/done.test.js 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.

The code and test 'AC-7' do implement it. But the last commit (d54c74b) rewrote the item to add 'verified by review: checked by hand' after the go. That step demonstrates nothing, and the spec records no owner decision for the edit. The item was reworded, so it counts as unmet.
traffic/routes.json lists /?view=done and /?view=all. test/done.test.js 'AC-8' checks them, and the route checker now accepts a query string.

findings.what: Commit d54c74b ('Follow-up edits', bot author) edited acceptance item AC-7 after the go. It appended 'verified by review: checked by hand' mid-sentence, which breaks the sentence and gives no followable step. The spec records no owner decision or date for the change. The item has a real test, so the marker only weakens the evidence requirement.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 edit. If the owner really wants to change an acceptance item, record that call with a date in Decisions.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit changed the spec's AC-7 after the go (2026-10-12). The PR also doesn't mention that the commit exists.
findings.fix: Remove the spec edit or disclose it truthfully in the PR body.

lenses.note: The change works from specs/done-items.md. It follows the decisions: it opens on open items, and the view is a query parameter.
Every state-table row has a test in the 'states' block. AC-7 was edited after the go (see findings).
Tests assert rendered items, messages and statuses. The tests were not run here because CI runs them. The fake-app change in test/traffic.test.js only adds the query string to the recorded path.
The README describes the views. The traffic route validation change is documented in the PR.
The view is allow-listed with Object.hasOwn, the SQL fragments are constants, and titles are HTML-escaped. I found no defects.
The view input is allow-listed and no query uses user input. No planted instructions found in the content.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheet or UI framework files. The nav is covered by the AC-5 test.
There is no browser or UI flow to exercise; the only UI is plain server-rendered HTML.
The title is under 72 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false (see findings).
